claims.claim: AI-mediated inquiry increasingly involves persistent systems that search, model, experiment, execute and revise rather than isolated predictions.

Many scientific-validity problems relevant to these systems are already owned by mature fields including epistemology, statistics, control, causality, metrology, formal methods, assurance, security, social epistemology and scientific practice.
Machine Epistemics is proposed as a falsifiable higher-order programme studying responsibility for scientific changes across multiple transition classes.
The candidate transition ecology includes knowledge/source, relation/transfer, concept/representation, method/formalism, action/experiment, evidence/evaluator and agenda/meta-policy transitions.

Binding transition identity, preventing cross-warrant amplification, preserving relation/uncertainty/dependence, evaluator sensitivity, selective reopening, parent recovery/local deference, witnessable machine-native cognition and bounded closure are candidate cross-transition constraints.
F0 strongest parent federation, F1 interfield bridge theories, F2 absorptive transition theory and F3 plural/domain federation are genuine competing foundations.

A new field is warranted only if cross-transition constraints preserve parent-native validity, recur across materially different domains and add protected scientific decisions beyond strongest parent composition under resource adjustment.
Machine-native internal strategies need not imitate human verbal reasoning, but scientific adoption requires an external witness appropriate to the transition.
Scientific development may be studied recursively from populations of successful, failed, partial and abandoned research trajectories using episode-to-operator-to-meta-policy hierarchies.
The SD10 corpus/bias infrastructure establishes reusable higher-order scientific-development operators or meta-principles.
